subject: Having issue trying to get plot to have plain-white background

messages.author: 0bde143813deb68c
messages.subject: Having issue trying to get plot to have plain-white background
parts:
Hi all,

I need to save plots for a publication but can not seem to get he syntax correct to have GGPLOT use only a white background vs. the default gray one.

I have tried the various themes but nothing seems to work.
This is the existing code for the plot and followed by what I have tried to no avail.

Works with gray plot frame backgrounds


ggplot(polished, aes(x =Night, y = Time, colour = Species)) +
                geom_point() +
             scale_colour_hue(l=40)+
              ggtitle(label = ' Linderos temporal activity')+
facet_grid(. ~ Night) +  facet_wrap(facets = ~Species)+
                scale_y_continuous(labels = label_hours, breaks = break_hours) +

                theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 270))

trying theme bw does not seem to work!
I did also load one of the "themes" packages to see if that was the issue.  Not.

 

ggplot(polished, aes(x =Night, y = Time, colour = Species)) +

                geom_point() +

               scale_colour_hue(l=40)+

              ggtitle(label = 'Temporal activty')+

facet_grid(. ~ Night) +  facet_wrap(facets = ~Species)+

                scale_y_continuous(labels = label_hours, breaks = break_hours) + 

      theme_bw(axis.text.x=element_text(angle = 270))

Any guidance on correct syntax/usage to plot clean-white plot back ground  welcomed.

Bruce

messages.subject: Re: Having issue trying to get plot to have plain-white background
parts:
Bruce--
You might want theme_classic()
see the examples down the page at:
https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggtheme.html 
You may need to add to that basic theme to get the facetting the way you want via + theme()

An alternative is to look at the additional themes in  https://rpubs.com/Koundy/71792 which demonstrated specifying a theme theme_Publication().
If you don't want the major grid lines, change panel.grid.major to element_blank()

Note that some journals actually specify a ggplot2 theme (or have their own custom theme) for figures in submitted manuscripts.,

messages.author: 942ffec526d6a312
messages.subject: Re: Having issue trying to get plot to have plain-white background
parts:
Hi Bruce,

I think because theme_bw is a 'complete' theme it doesn't support
many options. When I try, using the iris dataset, to do something
vaguely like your example:

ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, colour = Species))+
geom_point() + theme_bw(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 270))

I get:
Error in theme_bw(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 270)) :
unused argument (axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 270))

Is this what you are seeing?

I believe you could do it by modifying the appropriate bits in theme(),
but I tend to do something along the lines of:

ggplot(iris,aes(x = Sepal.Length,y = Sepal.Width,colour = Species))+
geom_point() + theme_bw() +

You might then want to add strip.background = element_blank() to the
theme call, if you don't want the facet strips to be grey either.

Hope this helps.

Ron.
